reproducibility_floor.note: one instance vs another on the same item, same model, same scaffold. Any ensemble gain smaller than this spread is noise.

verdict.statement: 3 instances as one model: naive majority 75.9%, blind no-abstain selector 89.7%, independent third-party panel 89.7%, best single instance 88.5%, oracle ceiling 92.0%. Neither the naive nor the judged ensemble separates from a single instance: the judged ensemble is +1.1pp against the best single instance and every paired test is above .05. The naive majority looks catastrophic only because a 3-way split forces it to abstain and abstention is scored as failure — a blind selector that never abstains reaches 89.7% on the same items. The judged panel is 89.7%, i.e. +0.0pp versus blind at paired exact p=1.0000, which is NOT distinguishable from blind selection — so the panel advantage is an abstention artefact, not judging skill. Only 2.3pp separates the judged selector from an oracle that reads the answer key.

judge_control.note: random_pick_expected_accuracy is the mean chance level of picking one of the three candidates uniformly. A panel below it is worse than chance; a panel above it is extracting signal.

discriminative_items.note: A split where every candidate is correct cannot reward a better selector, and one where none is cannot either. The tie-breaking task is only measurable on `discriminative` items.

position_sensitivity.note: A high flip rate is only harmful where the candidates differ in quality. On this bank 10 of 15 split items had all three candidates correct, so most flips swap between interchangeable answers. The one informative item (ifr-words-6) was flipped by @high from a wrong instance to the correct one — by luck, not skill.
position_sensitivity.power_caveat: n is 10 pairs. The 95% interval is wide enough that this is suggestive, not established.
